newsitem.title: USA: Brent crude dips in light U.S. paper dealings.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude dips in light U.S. paper dealings.

text.p: North Sea Brent crude oil dipped in late U.S. paper trading on Monday, traders said.
Activity was light as a result of a bank holiday in London, traders said.
Five July Brent partial cargoes changed hands, three times at $18.12 a barrel and one each at $18.10 and $18.11.
The July contract on London's International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) settled at $18.14 last Friday.
June/July Brent traded at minus 14 cents a barrel, a penny higher than the last intermonth transaction in Friday's late U.S. dealings.
The IPE reopens on Tuesday for a regular session.
